fields.title: What makes up time
fields.keyTakeaway: Time is made up of work, transit, and transfer, and on a mobile client, the number of network hops is often more expensive than everything happening on the server.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A screen opens in 2.8 seconds. What makes up that time?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Blind optimization wastes weeks on a component that accounts for 5% of the time. Breaking it down by steps takes a day and usually shows that 70% of the time is in one place no one thought about.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: The [[request-path|request path]] from tap to result:
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/items/0: **Client-side processing**—reaction to tap, preparing the request. Usually single-digit milliseconds.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/items/1: **[[connection-setup|Connection setup]]**—if no connection exists, it is established. On mobile networks, this is 100–300 ms before the first byte is sent.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/items/2: **Network to server**—[[round-trip-time|round-trip time]]. From 10 ms in the city to 300 ms on poor mobile coverage.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/items/3: **Server-side processing**—what is usually optimized: database queries, service calls, response assembly.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/items/4: **Response transfer**—depends on size. 500 KB on a slow network takes seconds.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/items/5: **Client-side rendering**—parsing the response, building the screen.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: What usually dominates this, contrary to expectations:
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: *Number of network hops.* Four sequential requests on a mobile network mean at least a second just for travel time, regardless of server speed. *Response size.* An 800 KB response instead of 80 KB adds seconds on a slow network. *[[cold-start|Cold start]].* The first open after app launch is the slowest: connections are not established, caches are empty.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: Three metrics worth distinguishing on the client:
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **[[ttfb|TTFB]]**—when the server started responding. Shows the server-side part. **[[time-to-render|Time to render]]**—when content appeared. **[[time-to-interactive|Time to interactive]]**—when the screen becomes usable. This is what the user actually experiences, and it can be twice the render time.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The team's expectation was that time was spent on the server. It turned out the server-side part was 42%, while 43% went to transit and transfer.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Hence the solution from `IN2-N1-L2`: one endpoint instead of six. It removed 600 ms on the network and allowed the server to gather data in parallel, cutting another 700 ms. Plus reducing the response to 90 KB. Total result—1.4 seconds, and most of the gains were not code optimization.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Breaking things down in environment copies distorts the picture: the network is faster, there is less data. Measurements must be taken on real users' real devices.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Time is made up of work, transit, and transfer, and on a mobile client, the number of network hops is often more expensive than everything happening on the server.
